Your course materials don't cover redox, so I'll teach this from general chemistry. The usual method is half-reactions, and it starts with one idea: electrons lost in oxidation must equal electrons gained in reduction.

Take a simple example: $\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{Ce}^{4+} \to \text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{Ce}^{3+}$.

Look at the oxidation state of each element before and after the reaction. Which species is losing electrons, and which is gaining them?
